name: Dev Studio UI — authorial rebuild ("the sea, actually moving")

evidence.reason: The PRD states the product's job in one sentence (§1 Resumo executivo), and README.md gives a one-line description of the site/library. Persona §7.1 also carries a one-sentence JTBD for the primary user.
evidence.quote: Seu trabalho principal é: > Encontrar um componente, experimentar seus estados e tokens, combiná-lo com outros componentes e exportar código reproduzível.

evidence.reason: The PRD names the product bet (evolve from an effects library into a 'component workbench', with Components/Playground/Studio as the core and the 24 Canvas components preserved; risk table: 'Component workbench é o núcleo'). DESIGN.md §3 derives the surface/navigation decisions directly from that bet ('Duas caixas, uma navegação: Components — a biblioteca … Uso diário. Effects — os 24 Canvas … intocado'; 'Preview é o padrão'), and commit bodies (43c4ddd navigation order 'Screens lead, then Components (the daily library), then Effects'; f4ecc35 'a screen gallery whose files must be assembled by hand has not delivered a screen') tie concrete design choices to the workbench promise and PRD principles/metrics (preview-first, no infinite loading).
evidence.quote: Duas caixas, uma navegação: **Components** — a biblioteca: 62 shadcn (Base UI) + React Bits. Uso diário. **Effects** — os 24 Canvas. Efeitos de página, fluxo do Playground, intocado.

evidence.reason: ENTRY uses a standard top nav (logo left, links centre, search/theme right), centred hero with one primary and one secondary CTA; DISCOVERY uses a familiar docs sidebar with grouped links, filter tabs, a search box and a 3-column card grid. The novelty (live canvas effects inside cards/demo) is the product itself and is confined to content areas.

Constraints are recorded before the build commits (PRD and DEPENDENCY-POLICY dated 2026-08-12; all build commits are 2026-08-13). Stack: README (Next.js 16, Tailwind v4, Cloudflare Workers), DEPENDENCY-POLICY pins exact versions (DialKit 1.4.3, Sandpack 2.20.0, MCP SDK 1.29.0, shadcn/React Bits snapshot SHAs, Node 22 Windows/Linux). PRD §14 RNFs fix browser support, WCAG 2.2 AA, perf budgets (+10% max regression), coverage thresholds; §6 non-goals and §15.6 'Não será instalada outra camada de skills nesta fase'. Design-system constraints: DESIGN.md (semantic tokens only, Geist Sans/Mono, six-step type scale, 4px spacing base, radius ladder). Team/time constraints are less explicit (phased plan in §17 and external gates in HANDOFF rather than calendar dates), but stack and design-system constraints are thoroughly recorded.
evidence.quote: | DialKit | Control and motion engine | `1.4.3` exact | MIT | … | Sandpack | React preview runtime | `2.20.0` exact | … Dependency upgrades require tests, coverage, lint and a production build on Node 22 for Windows and Linux.

evidence.reason: Decision rationale is recorded in three places: docs/solutions/ holds one note per solved problem with Problem / Solution / Principle / Known cost sections (8 notes across build, sandbox-preview, url-state); commit bodies explain why (e.g. 781d086 on why the hero image is served locally and why the swell only runs on-screen; e0db3b6 on why axe specs exclude the sandbox frame; ee06de4 on why React Bits capabilities are not derived from declared deps); DESIGN.md states rationale for each visual rule and declares itself a contract with a change-log discipline. AUDIT-MATRIX.md records the phase C correction (claimed 164/166 previews were not verified).
evidence.quote: ## Princípio — Um status derivado só vale se for derivado do artefato final, não da intenção do gerador. E o teste que prova o status tem que exercitar o artefato — `expect(código).toContain(...)` prova que escrevemos texto, `expect(parse(código)).toHaveNoErrors()` prova que escrevemos código.

evidence.reason: On ENTRY the filled white pill 'Get started →' is the single primary action; 'Browse components' is a plain text/ghost button beside it (outlined on mobile). Same pattern in the closing section. On DISCOVERY/DETAIL the only filled button is 'Playground' in the sidebar, and on INTERACTION 'Back to Docs' (the filled 'Start free' buttons visible are inside the sample demo content).

ENTRY reads 1) large two-line headline, 2) grey subhead, 3) CTA pair, 4) demo card with big '24' / '100%' figures. DISCOVERY reads title 'Components' → description → filter tabs → cards; DETAIL reads 'Glass' title → description → 'Demo image' → 'Install'. Size, weight and vertical position alone number the targets.

Sidebar links sit tightly under their group labels (Getting Started / Components / Effects) with larger gaps between groups; each card keeps thumbnail, title and description together inside a bordered card; the INTERACTION panel groups the 11 sliders under a 'Controls' label separate from the Copy for AI / Share block.

The hero headline on ENTRY is surrounded by ~100px of empty space above and generous margins on both sides, far more than around the stat cards or the install row; the sample page in INTERACTION does the same around 'Ship in days, not quarters.'

The palette is near-monochrome; the high-contrast white fill acts as the action colour and appears only on primary buttons (Get started, Playground, Back to Docs) and active nav/tab pills. The only chromatic elements are the blue swatch next to 'Color #425bff' (a value readout) and a decorative nebula background at the foot of ENTRY.

evidence.reason: Complexity is layered: catalog cards give a thumbnail + one-line summary and link to a DETAIL page; DETAIL shows one install command with package-manager/framework tabs and defers the full source ('Or copy the source below') and the tuning panel behind a 'Controls' button; INTERACTION keeps Copy for AI and Share as collapsed dropdowns.

Only hover and focus states were captured (focus ring on the logo and on the search button); no click/press state was captured for the copy buttons, Reset, sliders or Copy for AI, so immediate feedback after an action cannot be verified from the material.

The canvas/WebGL effects and playground are non-trivial to initialise, and the design shows a designed fallback toast ('You're seeing the fallback rendering…'), but no loading/skeleton state was captured on any surface, so a designed loading state cannot be confirmed.
No form is present on any surface; the only inputs are a search box and range sliders/colour picker in the playground, none of which have a submission or validation rule.

No destructive action (delete, remove, irreversible change) is visible; the only candidate is the low-stakes 'Reset' link in the playground controls, which returns ephemeral slider values to defaults.

The first 1440×900 screen states the value in one line, gives a primary 'Get started' CTA, and already shows a live demo card with '24 components', '100% open source' and a one-command install string with copy button, so core value is reached without scrolling. Mobile first screen shows headline, CTA pair and the demo card too.
The DISCOVERY catalog has a search input and filter tabs that can produce a no-results state, but no empty state was captured in any screenshot, so its content cannot be judged.

Help appears at the point of doubt: the fallback toast explains why the effect is not rendering and supplies the exact flag with a copy button; DETAIL adds the inline hint 'Move the lens over the photo to magnify every detail.' under 'Demo image'; the search palette shows an 'esc' hint; the install card is labelled 'ONE COMMAND'. No tour is used.
No multi-step flow (wizard, checkout, onboarding sequence) exists on any captured surface.
No testimonials or quotes appear on any surface; the ENTRY footer only lists library credits ('Canvas UI — David Haz', 'React Bits — David Haz').

Numbers used as proof are specific and verifiable within the product: ENTRY shows '24 Components — and counting' and '100% Open source — free forever'; DISCOVERY tabs show 'Custom · 24 / Shadcn · 62 / React Bits · 166' and the catalog indeed renders 24 cards; the footer states the licences (MIT + Commons Clause, MIT). No vague 'thousands of users' claims.

There is no pricing or signup decision point on any surface (the product is presented as free and open source; 'Get started' leads to docs). The 'Sign in / Start free' buttons visible on INTERACTION belong to the sample demo page, not the product.
No surface collects user data: there are no account, payment or contact forms, only a search box and playground sliders.
